hints: Start by drawing the two structures side by side and look for the key difference in their carbon skeletons.
Recall that alkaline aqueous iodine tests for the special group $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, which gives a yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$.
Check which diol contains that methyl plus adjacent alcohol unit, then confirm the other three reagents would react the same way with both diols.
walkthrough:
**Draw both diols**

Look closely at what you have. This is the key to the whole question.

$$\text{propane-1,2-diol} = \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$$
$$\text{ethane-1,2-diol} = \text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Spot the iodoform unit**

Remember the iodoform (tri-iodomethane) test. Alkaline aqueous iodine gives a yellow precipitate only with $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ groups.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}- + \text{I}_2 / \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 \text{(yellow ppt)}$$

**Apply to these two compounds**

Propane-1,2-diol has $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so it gives a positive result with a pale yellow precipitate. Ethane-1,2-diol has only $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ groups and no methyl group, so it stays as a brown solution with no precipitate. That is a clear distinction.

options.A: Correct. Only propane-1,2-diol contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit needed for the iodoform reaction, so it forms yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate with alkaline aqueous iodine while ethane-1,2-diol does not.
options.B: Both diols contain primary and/or secondary alcohol groups, so both are oxidised by acidified dichromate(VI) with the same orange to green colour change. No distinction is seen.
options.C: Ethanol with concentrated sulfuric acid is for ester formation with carboxylic acids. Neither compound is a carboxylic acid, and both have -OH groups that behave similarly, so this is not a distinguishing test.
options.D: Sodium metal reacts with any -OH group to give hydrogen gas: $2\text{ROH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RONa} + \text{H}_2$. Since both molecules have two -OH groups, both give effervescence.
